about: What the analyzers need in a log, and which LOG_BITMASK bits log it (spec: Analyzers common to all vehicles, 'Logging adequacy'). A message the log lacks while none of its bits is set is a logging gap with a parameter fix, which sets the 'add' bit; one that is missing although a bit is set has another cause, which the analyzer that needs it reports. Bits are per vehicle, read from the release's source; a vehicle not listed is not checked for them yet.

source.copter: ArduCopter/defines.h MASK_LOG_* and the logging loops in ArduCopter/Copter.cpp, at Copter-4.7.0 (1511f27)

needs.for: IMU error counts and accelerometer data
system health: loop timing and CPU load
filter phase lag and rate tuning

raw_gyro.about: INS_RAW_LOG_OPT bits, from libraries/AP_InertialSensor/AP_InertialSensor.h RAW_LOGGING_OPTION at 4.7.0. GYR holds pre-filter samples unless 'post filter' is set without 'pre and post filter'; with 'pre and post filter' the post-filter samples are logged as instance + the number of gyros.

fast_notch.about: A harmonic notch that follows ESC RPM, an RPM sensor, throttle or the in-flight FFT moves at 200 Hz, or at the loop rate with option bit 2. Its inputs (FTN, FTNS) and centres (FCN, FCNS) are logged at 10 Hz unless this LOG_BITMASK bit logs them at every update; without it the filter model rebuilds what the notch followed from rows the log holds less often (ESC RPM at 100 Hz), and cannot replay it exactly. The bit makes logs much larger, so it is for filter test flights.

tune.about: The tune check measures the rate loop from RATE and the rate PIDs (PIDR, PIDP, PIDY). With LOG_BITMASK bit 0 (fast attitude) RATE is logged every loop, and the PIDs too with bit 12; without bit 0 both are logged at 10 Hz. Copter's default bitmask sets bits 1 and 12 but not 0. Bits 0 and 12 are proposed for the tune-check flight only, with raw IMU logging (bit 19) off for it to keep the logging bandwidth for them, and no logging rate cap.

rate_limit.about: LOG_FILE_RATEMAX and LOG_BLK_RATEMAX cap every streaming message of their backend at that many a second; 0 turns the cap off. Streaming messages are those whose log structure is marked so, or written with WriteStreaming: raw IMU (GYR, ACC), IMU, VIBE, RATE, ATT, PIDR/P/Y, ESC, RCOU, MOTB, CTUN, BAT, and the notch inputs FTN and FTNS. The rate, attitude and PID messages are logged every loop, raw IMU at the gyro rate, so a cap below either thins the data the analyzers need.
rate_limit.source: libraries/AP_Logger/AP_Logger_Backend.cpp AP_Logger_RateLimiter::should_log and LogStructure streaming flags; LOG_*_RATEMAX in libraries/AP_Logger/AP_Logger.cpp (default 0), at 4.7.0

buffer.about: A logger that drops messages may keep up with a bigger write buffer (LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE, KiB, 4 to 200; read at start-up). The app raises it by at most step_kib, only while the flight's lowest free memory (PM.Mem) leaves keep_free_kib to spare. App rules, uncalibrated.

filter_settings.about: What a filter check depends on: once a flight of the airframe has been checked with raw gyro data, the raw-gyro and fast-notch diagnostics are not proposed again while these parameters and the airframe's build stay the same. Learned values (MOT_THST_HOVER) are left out: they change on every flight.
